question.text: A vehicle A moves with an acceleration of 2 m/s² towards the east, while a vehicle B accelerates at 4 m/s² towards the north. Determine the relative acceleration of vehicle B as observed from vehicle A.
conditions: car A accelerates at 2 m/s² due east
car B accelerates at 4 m/s² due north
motion occurs in a horizontal plane

solution.approach: Relative acceleration is the vector difference of the two accelerations, found by adding the perpendicular east and north components.

steps.text: Write the two accelerations as vectors along east and north.
Find the magnitude of the resultant.
Find the direction using the two perpendicular components, −2 (west) and 4 (north).
steps.equation: tan α = 4/2 = 2 → α = tan⁻¹(2) ≈ 63.4°, measured from west towards north

final_answer.value: a_(B/A) = 2√5 m/s² ≈ 4.47 m/s², directed about 63.4° north of west (equivalently about 26.6° west of north)

common_mistakes.text: Adding a_A and a_B instead of subtracting gives a_(B/A) = (2î + 4ĵ), a different direction, north-east instead of north-west.
Computing the magnitude as 4 − 2 = 2 m/s² by treating the two accelerations as if they were along the same line, ignoring that they are perpendicular.
